title: Lab 12 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Unknown ID Part 3 — Quick Strep and nucleic acid tests

questions.prompt: What does the Quick Strep test detect?

options.text: Streptococcus pyogenes cell wall antigens
Antibodies the patient made against S. pyogenes
S. pyogenes DNA sequences
Beta-hemolysis on blood agar

questions.explanation: Labeling area: mobile colored bead-labeled antibodies specific for S. pyogenes cell wall antigens. Test area: immobilized antibodies for those antigens.

why.B: Quick Strep is an antigen detection test.
why.C: That would be a nucleic acid test.

questions.prompt: In the Quick Strep test, what does the extraction solution (Reagent 1 + Reagent 2) do?

options.text: Kills the bacteria so they're safe to culture
Dissolves cell wall antigens from the swab sample
Stains the bacteria purple
Amplifies Strep DNA

questions.explanation: The extraction solution dissolves cell wall antigens so they flow up the dipstick.

why.A: Its job is to release the antigens.
why.D: Quick Strep is antibody-based, not nucleic acid.

questions.prompt: After inserting the Quick Strep dipstick into the extraction solution, how long do you wait before reading it?

options.text: 10 seconds
5 minutes
1 minute
24 hours

questions.explanation: Rotate the swab 10 times, leave it 1 minute, squeeze it out, then insert the dipstick and wait 5 minutes.

why.A: Ten revolutions is the swab step, not the read time.
why.C: 1 minute is how long the swab sits in the solution.

questions.prompt: A Quick Strep dipstick shows a control line but no test line. What is the result?

options.text: Negative
Positive
Invalid
Positive for a non-Strep pathogen

questions.explanation: Control line only = negative. No control line = invalid.

why.B: Positive shows both the control and test lines.
why.C: A control line is present, so it's valid.
why.D: The test only detects S. pyogenes antigens.

questions.prompt: A Quick Strep dipstick shows no control line. What should you conclude?

options.text: Invalid — the test didn't run correctly
Negative for S. pyogenes
Positive for S. pyogenes
Positive if there is a test line

questions.explanation: The control area's immobilized antibodies bind excess color-labeled antibodies; with no control line, the result is invalid.

why.B: A negative needs a visible control line.
why.C: Without the control line, no result can be trusted.
why.D: Any result without a control line is invalid.

questions.prompt: In a positive Quick Strep test, what is captured at the test line?

options.text: S. pyogenes antigen bound to a colored, bead-labeled antibody
Free colored beads with no antigen
The patient's own antibodies against Strep
Fluorescent DNA strands

questions.explanation: The labeled antibody binds the antigen, and immobilized antibodies at the test area capture that complex, making a colored line.

why.B: Excess labeled antibodies are caught at the control line.
why.C: This test detects antigen, not patient antibodies.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of nucleic acid identification tests?

options.text: They find pathogen DNA/RNA without culture, possibly before antibodies are detectable
They are the cheapest tests and need no special equipment
They require a pure culture grown for 48 hours
They detect the patient's antibodies to the pathogen

questions.explanation: Nucleic acid tests are sensitive and specific, need no culture, and may detect infection before antibodies are detectable.

why.B: They tend to be expensive and need special equipment.

questions.prompt: Put the array-based nucleic acid test steps in order.

options.text: Label → wash → heat → hybridize to probes → compare
Hybridize to probes → heat → label → compare → wash
Heat → label → hybridize to probes → wash → compare
Wash → heat → hybridize to probes → label → compare

questions.explanation: Heat to separate DNA strands, label them, let them hybridize (complementary base pairing) to known probes, wash away unpaired strands, then compare the label pattern to the database.

why.A: Strands must be separated by heat first.
why.B: Washing removes unpaired strands before reading.

questions.prompt: In the nucleic acid probe simulation, probe 1 (human DNA) should always light up. Why?

options.text: It means the patient is infected with HIV
It's the negative control for the test
It's the positive control (blood contains human DNA)
It detects the Hepatitis B virus

questions.explanation: Probe 1 = human DNA (positive control). It confirms the test is working.

why.B: A negative control shouldn't light up.

questions.prompt: In the nucleic acid simulation, a blood sample's labeled sequence pairs with probe 4. What does the patient have?

options.text: West Nile virus
Syphilis
Hepatitis C virus
Malaria

questions.explanation: Key: 1 human DNA (+ control), 2 Hep B, 3 West Nile, 4 malaria, 5 Hep C, 6 syphilis, 7 HIV.

questions.prompt: In the nucleic acid simulation, why are unpaired blood sample sequences removed ('rinsed')?

options.text: So only sequences that hybridized to a probe give a signal
To remove the human DNA control
To make the probes fluorescent
To separate DNA strands before labeling

questions.explanation: Washing removes unpaired strands so the remaining labels show only true complementary matches.

why.B: Human DNA pairs with probe 1 and should remain.
why.C: The blood sample sequences carry the label.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an example use of nucleic acid identification tests?

options.text: Quick Strep dipstick
Catalase test with hydrogen peroxide
Original COVID-19 nasopharyngeal PCR tests
Kirby-Bauer sensitivity testing

questions.explanation: Examples: various STI pathogens, food poisoning pathogens, Giardia in stool, bioterrorism agents, original COVID-19 PCR tests.

questions.prompt: This dipstick diagram labels three zones. Where are the mobile, colored bead-labeled antibodies?

options.text: The control area at the top (C)
The test area in the middle
The labeling area, near where the sample enters
The absorbent pad at the very top

questions.explanation: Labeling area: mobile colored antibodies. Test area: immobilized antibodies to S. pyogenes antigens. Control area: immobilized antibodies that bind excess labeled antibodies.

why.A: The control area holds immobilized antibodies for excess labels.
why.B: The test area holds immobilized antibodies for the antigen.
why.D: The pad only soaks up leftover sample.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation of nucleic acid identification tests?

options.text: They require growing the organism in culture first
They can't detect organisms that are hard to culture
They are less specific than antibody tests
They tend to be expensive and need special equipment and training

questions.explanation: Limitations: expensive, special equipment, and possibly special training.

why.B: They're used for hard-to-culture STI pathogens.
why.C: They are described as sensitive and specific.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Quick Strep procedure is FALSE?

options.text: Gloves are worn
The swab is rotated 10 revolutions in the extraction solution
The swab, dipstick and vial go into the biohazard bag
The test reagents are discarded in the biohazard bag
The swab sample represents a throat swab specimen

questions.explanation: DO NOT discard the test reagents or the cardboard rack — only the swab, dipstick and plastic vial go in biohazard.

why.A: True — the slide says to wear gloves.
